ideas.name: NVIDIA Corporation
ideas.thesis: NVDA appeared in all 6 of 6 overnight screens with unanimous high conviction. The stock is historically cheap at ~25x forward earnings versus its pre-earnings historical range of 35-40x, while Wall Street consensus expects ~96% revenue growth and the average analyst price target of ~$304 implies ~35-40% upside from ~$218-$225. A defined-risk call spread (e.g., Aug 29 expiry $230/$260) is the preferred structure: it captures the blowout earnings setup while limiting downside from a potential sell-the-news reaction if Warsh delivers a hawkish Jackson Hole surprise just 36 hours after the print.
ideas.catalyst: Q2 FY2027 earnings report after market close on August 26, 2026; followed by Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote on August 28
ideas.edge: Trading at ~25x forward P/E vs. historical pre-earnings range of 35-40x; re-rate to 30x alone implies ~20% upside; consensus analyst PT ~$304 vs. ~$220 current (~35-40% gap); 85% of 68 analysts rated Buy; revenue estimates revised +6.67% over past 3 months; options market pricing 5%+ implied move
ideas.bull_case: NVDA beats on ~96% revenue growth expectations, guides strongly on HBM/Blackwell demand, and the stock re-rates toward the 30-35x forward P/E range, with the call spread capturing a rapid move toward $260+.
ideas.bear_case: Even a clean beat triggers sell-the-news given elevated positioning, and a hawkish Warsh speech 36 hours later compresses tech multiples further — the call spread expires worthless but caps maximum loss to premium paid.

ideas.name: SK Hynix Inc. (ADR)
ideas.thesis: SKHY appeared in all 6 of 6 overnight screens with unanimous high conviction. As NVIDIA's primary HBM4 memory supplier, SKHY is the purest liquid US-listed proxy for AI infrastructure demand, and the NVDA August 26 earnings print is a direct re-rating catalyst for the entire memory stack. A 40 trillion KRW share buyback announced August 20 provides a near-term price floor, Temasek sovereign wealth fund investment adds validation, and the stock trades at a deep discount — ~11x TTM P/E with 257% YoY revenue growth — against a BofA price target of $250 implying ~54% upside from ~$162.
ideas.catalyst: 40 trillion KRW share buyback announced August 20, 2026; NVDA earnings read-through on August 26; imminent US-South Korea tech supply contract announcements tied to South Korean presidential San Francisco visit
ideas.edge: Consensus analyst PT ~$245-$250 vs. current ~$162-$164 = ~54-57% implied upside; trading at ~11x TTM P/E with 257% YoY revenue growth and 76% operating margins; BofA reiterated Buy August 20; HBM memory fully allocated through 2027; buyback provides price floor
ideas.bull_case: NVDA posts a blowout quarter, explicitly highlights HBM supply allocation through 2027, and SKHY re-rates sharply toward the $200-$250 analyst target range; the buyback absorbs any dip and signals management confidence at current levels.
ideas.bear_case: ADR gap risk on Korean exchange moves, a broader tech sell-off from hawkish Jackson Hole commentary, or any supply-chain concern mentioned on NVDA's call could pressure SKHY despite strong fundamentals; the stock already flushed 9-10% post-July earnings, showing binary event sensitivity.

ideas.name: Invesco QQQ Trust (Nasdaq-100 ETF)
ideas.thesis: QQQ appeared in 5 of 6 overnight screens as the consensus macro hedge vehicle. New Fed Chair Warsh's debut Jackson Hole keynote on August 28 — landing just 36 hours after the NVDA earnings print — creates a genuine two-way vol event: Warsh has signaled Fed independence from market pricing with three July FOMC dissenters already on record. With the 30-year yield at a multi-decade high of 5.25% and September hike odds around 1-in-3, a defined-risk QQQ put spread (e.g., Sep5 $490/$470) is a low-cost portfolio hedge against the macro tail that threatens the rest of this portfolio's tech-heavy exposure.
ideas.catalyst: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh debut Jackson Hole keynote on August 28, 2026; FOMC September 15-16 meeting with ~55/45 hike-vs-hold odds per CME FedWatch
ideas.edge: QQQ near all-time highs at ~Nasdaq 26,300 with 10-yr yield at 4.70% and 30-yr at 5.25%; a Sep hike historically reprices QQQ 5-8% lower; a $490/$470 put spread costs ~2-3% to protect a 6-8% drawdown scenario; straddle/strangle into Aug 26 close captures both NVDA and Warsh events
ideas.bull_case: Warsh strikes a balanced tone, September hike odds fade, NVDA earnings lift the Nasdaq, and QQQ makes new highs — put spread expires worthless but served its hedging purpose at a defined, modest cost.
ideas.bear_case: Warsh signals July-style hawkish independence, September hike is repriced above 50%, and rate-sensitive tech multiples compress 5-8% quickly — put spread pays out and offsets losses in NVDA/SKHY long exposure.

ideas.name: Apple Inc.
ideas.thesis: AAPL appeared in 2 of 6 overnight screens, just meeting the consensus threshold. The company posted its strongest-ever June quarter — $109.4B revenue (+16% YoY) and EPS of $2.02 (+29% YoY) — but the post-earnings stock reaction was muted, creating a gap between fundamental strength and price. In a macro environment where 30-year yields at 5.25% punish speculative growth, AAPL's durable, broad-based earnings across iPhone, Mac, and Services offer a quality anchor, with the September iPhone event as the next identifiable catalyst.
ideas.catalyst: Post-earnings drift window following best-ever June quarter reported ~2 weeks ago; September 2026 iPhone annual event (date TBD, typically early September)
ideas.edge: EPS $2.02 (+29% YoY), revenue $109.4B (+16% YoY) with double-digit growth across all geographies and segments; muted post-earnings price reaction creates a swing entry; stock at ~$310 offers GARP positioning in a high-yield environment
ideas.bull_case: The September iPhone event drives a product cycle narrative, muted post-earnings drift resolves upward as the market digests the strongest-ever June quarter, and AAPL's defensive earnings quality attracts rotation out of rate-sensitive speculative growth.
ideas.bear_case: At ~$310 with the 30-year yield at 5.25%, AAPL's premium valuation remains vulnerable to multiple compression if Warsh surprises hawkishly; the muted post-earnings reaction may signal the market is already pricing in a deceleration in Services growth.
